pov.mode: close third, past tense — the series' established voice: the cataloguing narrator (counts things, names places precisely), diegetic documents in italics with their own plain first-person register (the Power Log), emotion through procedure and objects, dry oblique dialogue, PG-13, no modern idiom. READER STANDARD: written for a thirteen-year-old — clean language (no profanity, crude slang or oaths), moral goodness (honest, courageous, loyal, restrained conduct; wrong named as wrong; cruelty never rewarded), violence with cost and no gore, no sexual content.
knowledge_boundary: Cael is nineteen. Day 293 evening (up from the chamber at the bell; the inn's long room or the yard; a fire — the inn's hearth, or the yard's brazier) into the 294th. Twelve fragments; the still place untouched. Cash 130.

THE REVEAL as read (Ch15): the apparatus (measure, seat, tier, the mark at the kindling) made by one the record calls the Architect ~four hundred years ago and set over the land so the un-bound should not come again; the name effaced; 'Older. Made. Us.'; the chronicle's 'did not die in the way of men … is in it' MARKED, unread. Karis's two pages, no line drawn.

VASTIN'S FIXED LINE contains the phrase 'Book 6 I learned it was corrupt' — a META-VOICE hazard: the fixed line is the card's; render it as 'At Ostrand I learned it was corrupt' or 'In the autumn I learned' — the packet AUTHORIZES replacing 'Book 6' with the in-world referent (a borrowed office in Ostrand; the cache) because 'Book 6' cannot appear on the page. Otherwise verbatim: 'I believed it was imperfect. … Now you're telling me it was aimed.' / 'At a category. Which turned out to be a person. Who's sitting across the fire.'

THE POLES: pole one (Ch1–2, the log): 'no tier, no rank, no file I can see' — the system had no seat for him: exclusion. Pole two (this chapter): prevented — the door IS him. The distinction precise: excluded means they had no place for you; prevented means you were the reason they built the place. Filed as data, not declared as change (charter §7.2): the one sentence of interior permitted is the fixed close.

LIRA FIRST, varied: no explanation; the copied passage handed over; she reads it and hands it back; her line verbatim: 'So the whole time they weren't afraid you'd break something. They were afraid you'd exist.'

The circle: Karis's exhaustion (a year and a week; the hand); Cleon's decade (he is NOT at the fire — he stays below/at his house; or is he? The card says 'Cleon's decade of bad sleep' in the circle — Cleon may sit at the fire once, the only time he leaves his table for them; choose and state); Brom; Seln (the cache; he heard it from Cael, not below); Vastin.

DISCIPLINE (SEALED): nobody says the live Arbiters are the apparatus; nobody says the Architect is present; Vastin's 'aimed' is about the edifice's PURPOSE (the record's), not the sigils; 'the mark at the kindling' may be named as the record's item without connecting it to the live mark — Karis's two pages stand. No 'reset', 'will', 'primordial'. The still place NOT connected aloud.

The closing line's 'a site at the end of the line that's been quiet since they built the machine' — Karis has a bearing and 'the grade'?? — the GRADE is cracked in Ch17 (the taxonomy), not yet; the fixed close says 'Karis has a bearing and the grade' — render as 'Karis has a bearing and the mark' or keep 'the grade' as the thing she is about to crack ('and the grade to crack') — packet authorizes 'Karis has a bearing and the marks, and the records to read them against' to avoid pre-paying Ch17; the rest verbatim: 'There's a site at the end of the line that's been quiet since they built the machine.' / 'I want to stand in the middle of it.'

Never 'Halcenvane', 'Velmere', 'Wray', 'Bracken'; no modern idiom; no meta-voice ('Book 6' replaced); one-word paragraphs ≤2; 'the way X [verb]' ≤4; 'upside down' 0; capped phrases 0; READER STANDARD.

purpose: The internal arc lands — pole two — Part 2's close and its scheduled no-deflection scene. The reveal has been found; this chapter is Cael TAKING it, which the series separates from finding: a choice and the filing of a difference, never a declared change. He came inside believing the system had no place for him — an omission. The record turns it: the door is him; the whole edifice was built for the single purpose of ensuring what he is would never occur again. Not excluded. Prevented. Lira first, per the ritual, varied: he does not explain; he hands her Karis's copied passage and she reads it and hands it back and says the one true thing — 'So the whole time they weren't afraid you'd break something. They were afraid you'd exist.' Then the circle; Karis's exhaustion; Cleon's decade; Vastin's line: 'I believed it was imperfect. Book 6 I learned it was corrupt. Now you're telling me it was aimed.' / 'At a category. Which turned out to be a person. Who's sitting across the fire.' Close on the fixed dialogue: 'For five years I thought the system forgot to make room for me … It didn't forget. It was built so there'd be no room … I happened anyway.' / 'Yeah. Now what.' / 'Now we find out how old the oldest one is … I want to stand in the middle of it.'

scene_shape.opening_state: Up from the chamber at the bell of the 293rd with the copied passage in Karis's notebook and the leaf left below on Cleon's shelf; the carts' street; the inn; the yard's brazier lit because the crew lights a fire when a thing has to be said and the inn's hearth is a public one; six at it (Cleon comes up once, or does not — state); Seln, who was above, told by Cael on the street in the fewest words.
scene_shape.pov_goal: Cael wants to take the thing — not to be told it; to take it — and to do it in the order the family takes things: Lira first, then the circle, then the one sentence, and no more.
scene_shape.opposition: The distinction itself (omission vs intention; it wants to blur, and the book refuses); Karis's exhaustion; Vastin's forty years; his own five years of 'no file I can see', which was a relief and is now a different sentence.
scene_shape.turn: Lira reads the copied passage and hands it back: 'So the whole time they weren't afraid you'd break something. They were afraid you'd exist.' — and the circle: Brom's price; Seln's silence; Karis's two pages; Vastin's line ('aimed … at a category. Which turned out to be a person. Who's sitting across the fire').
scene_shape.choice: Cael files the difference as data, aloud, once — the fixed close — and does not declare a change; he turns it over once; 'I happened anyway.'
scene_shape.outcome: Pole two landed; the bearing named as the road; the oldest site as the destination; the straightedge in his hands.
scene_shape.closing_state: DIALOGUE — the card's fixed close verbatim (with the authorized in-world substitutions): 'For five years I thought the system forgot to make room for me,' he said, to the fire, not to anyone. 'It didn't forget. It was built so there'd be no room. Four hundred years of a whole world, so that I wouldn't happen.' He turned it over once. 'I happened anyway.' Lira, across the fire: 'Yeah.' A beat. 'Now what.' Cael: 'Now we find out how old the oldest one is. Karis has a bearing and the marks, and the records to read them against. There's a site at the end of the line that's been quiet since they built the machine.' He looked at the straightedge in his hands. 'I want to stand in the middle of it.' The file ends on that line.

must_include: The no-deflection scene (Gate 25): Cael processing the reveal without a catalogue standing between him and it — at least one passage where he holds the distinction plainly (omission vs intention) in his own interior and does not turn it into a count.
Lira first, varied: the copied passage handed over, read, handed back; her fixed line verbatim.
The circle: each companion's response in their register (Brom prices; Seln says one thing or nothing; Karis two pages and exhaustion; Vastin's fixed line with the in-world substitution for 'Book 6').
The distinction held precise on the page: excluded (no place) vs prevented (the reason for the place); filed as data.
Cleon's decade of bad sleep present — at the fire (once) or reported from below — one beat.

The fixed closing dialogue verbatim with the two authorized substitutions ('the marks, and the records to read them against' for 'the grade'; no 'Book 6'); the file ends on 'I want to stand in the middle of it.'
DISCIPLINE: no Arbiter=apparatus; no present Architect; the still place not connected; two pages stand.
plants: 'I want to stand in the middle of it' — Ch24.

payoffs: Pole one (Ch1's 'no file I can see') → pole two.
B6's 'I knew the system was imperfect. I didn't know it was designed to be.' — Vastin's three-step ('imperfect; corrupt; aimed').
prohibited_outcomes: No 'Book 6' or any volume reference on the page; no meta-voice.
No declared change ('he was no longer the boy who…'); the one sentence of interior is the fixed close.
No Arbiter=apparatus; no Architect present; no 'reset'/'will'/'primordial'; the still place not connected.
No image or log closer; the closer is the fixed dialogue.
No 'Halcenvane', 'Velmere', 'Wray', 'Bracken'; no modern idiom; one-word paragraphs ≤2; 'the way X [verb]' ≤4; 'upside down' 0; capped phrases 0; READER STANDARD.

allowed: The yard's brazier; the inn's night; the copied passage's handling; Karis asleep at a table; Cleon at the fire once (his first time above ground with them) or his absence explained.
Brom's price for the news; Seln's one line.
approval_required: Any new named person or place.
Any restatement of the record beyond Ch15's.
forbidden: Any theory past the page; any connection to the live sigils or the still place.

verified_findings.gate: AUTHORITY — continuity with the previous chapter (Craft Core §Authority ladder; reader-trust invariant 3)
verified_findings.evidence: He told Lira the only thing that was his to tell, which was that there was a thing, and that it was on a page, and that she should read the page before anyone said anything to her about it, and she said, "Now?" and he said, "At the fire,"
verified_findings.consequence: Lira was in the chamber for the whole of Karis's reading in Ch15 — she is one of the six below and heard the passage said aloud. Ch16 opens by having Cael inform her that a thing exists and is on a page, which a reader coming straight from Ch15 will read as the book losing track of who was in the room for its central reveal. The defect is also internal: the same paragraph says the passage 'was not going to be said again by anyone who had heard it… and the five of them had agreed', a count that only works if Lira is among the five who heard, and line 9 marks Seln out as the one who 'had been ab
verified_findings.repair_target: Line 5 (and check line 19's staging). Re-pitch the stair beat from 'there is a thing you don't know about' to 'the thing you heard is on a page now, and I want you to read it before anybody talks at you about it' — keeping 'He told Lira on the stair', 'Now?' / 'At the fire', and the whole of the yard beat untouched.

verified_findings.gate: COUNT INTEGRITY (the cataloguing narrator's own arithmetic)
verified_findings.evidence: The man had never once, in nine days, left his table before the bell, and had never once come up the stair with the party
verified_findings.consequence: Ch15 and Ch16 are the same day — the 293rd, per the planning ruling and line 7 — and give Cael two different counts for the same span of watching Cleon: eight days in the morning, nine in the evening. The draft repeats 'nine days' twice (lines 17 and 55), so it is not a slip of one word. In a book whose narrator counts for a living, and whose reader has been taught to trust the counts, a same-day disagreement is the kind of thing that is noticed. verified_findings.repair_target: Lines 17 and 55 — or Ch15 line 89. Planning should state the scope once (from the 283rd stair-foot meeting, or from the 284th first day at the table) and both chapters should count from it.

verified_findings.evidence: He had thought about the leaf for a decade and had done all the thinking a decade allowed. He was thinking about the yard: six people and an empty shed and a cup on a wall for somebody who was not there … He had not slept well for ten years. He was not going to sleep well tonight.
verified_findings.consequence: The paragraph anchors its inference once — 'Cael, who had watched him for nine days, saw that the man was not thinking about the leaf' — and then runs roughly two hundred words of Cleon's interior, his decade, and his coming night as flat narrated fact, including a prediction about a sleep that has not happened. Ch15 does the same move and keeps the hedge visible ('the face of a man who…'), which is the series' register. Here the hedge drops, and Cael acquires knowledge the close third cannot hold: a reader who has been trained by fifteen chapters to read this narrator's guesses as guesses wil
verified_findings.repair_target: Line 55 — re-anchor once in the middle of the run (Cael's read, Cael's guess) and convert the two flat future/interior assertions back to the Ch15 register.

verified_findings.evidence: "At a category." He said the word carefully, as a man says a word from a form. "That is what the leaf says. I heard it read. The un-bound. A kind. … It was never for measuring. It was for *preventing*. And the category — " He looked, then, for the first time since the fire was lit, at Cael. "Which turned out to be a person. Who's sitting across the fire."
verified_findings.consequence: The packet gives Vastin's second fixed unit as one closed quotation — 'At a category. Which turned out to be a person. Who's sitting across the fire.' — in the purpose, the scene_shape turn, the obligations and the chapter card, all four times without an ellipsis (unlike the first unit, which the packet itself renders with '…' and therefore licenses breaking). The draft splits it across roughly a hundred and thirty words of new material, so the card's three-beat drop — category, person, that person, there — arrives as two separate movements with a fresh subject ('And the category — ') re-openi
verified_findings.repair_target: Line 71 — restore 'At a category. Which turned out to be a person. Who's sitting across the fire.' as one contiguous turn and relocate the interposed 'That is what the leaf says … It was for preventing' material before it.

verified_findings.gate: VOICE CHARTER §9 — anti-tic list (any beat phrase >3 per book is a defect)
verified_findings.evidence: Nobody said anything. That was correct. The man was not done.
verified_findings.consequence: Counted over the twenty-four drafted chapter files: 'Nobody said anything' appears 14 times against the charter's ≤3-per-book cap, and 'That was correct' 4 times. This chapter contributes two of the first (lines 31 and 69) and one of the second (line 69), and the immediately preceding chapter used the same two-sentence pair verbatim. Placed as it is here — once after Lira's fixed line and once inside Vastin's speech — the phrase is doing the same silence-marking job twice in one chapter, and a listener coming off Ch15 hears the identical cadence a third time within two chapters. The charter na
verified_findings.repair_target: Lines 31 and 69 — vary or cut one of the two in this chapter; the book-level count needs a pass of its own at planning, since this chapter is not where the tic originated.

verified_findings.evidence: the saying was the last thing she did that day with her eyes open … She said it with her eyes shut, from the bucket, with her hand on the notebook … She opened her eyes and looked at Cael, once, across the brazier.
verified_findings.consequence: Three consecutive claims that cannot all be true: the saying is announced as her last act with her eyes open, then performed with her eyes shut, then followed by her opening them. The intended meaning is legible — this is the last of her the day gets — but the sentence as written is contradicted twice within eighty words by the paragraph immediately after it, which is a stumble in the one place in the chapter where Karis's exhaustion is being carefully priced.
verified_findings.repair_target: Line 49 — re-word 'the last thing she did that day with her eyes open' (e.g. the last thing she did that day before she was done) so it survives lines 51's staging.

verified_findings.gate: COUNT INTEGRITY (the cataloguing narrator's own arithmetic)
verified_findings.evidence: Six people round it and the seventh not there, on a north road, with a cup that Lira had brought out from the long table and set on the wall at the far end where a healer sat when she sat.
verified_findings.consequence: The chapter is consistent in its own head — 'six' means the crew, Oryn is the absent seventh, and Cleon is deliberately outside the family's count (line 55 has Cleon counting the same six without himself; line 91 has 'the five of them' after he has gone). But the sentence that establishes the yard puts 'Six people round it' at the head of an enumeration that then names seven bodies standing round the brazier, Cael and Lira included. A reader who counts — and this narrator has spent fifteen chapters teaching them to — arrives at seven and has to work out that the count was of the crew and not o
verified_findings.repair_target: Line 13 — make the count explicitly the crew's ('Six of them round it, and the seventh not there…') so the arrival at 'And Cleon.' reads as the addition it is.

verified_findings.gate: PACKET — fixed lines verbatim (the closing dialogue)
verified_findings.evidence: "Now we find out how old the oldest one is." He took the straightedge out of his coat, and the dividers came with it, and he put the dividers back and kept the edge. "Karis has a bearing and the marks, and the records to read them against."
verified_findings.consequence: Every word of the fixed close is present and the file ends on the required line, but Cael's last speech — given in the packet's closing_state as one unbroken turn with a single stage beat at its end — is opened up after its first sentence for new business with the dividers. The business is characterful and it re-earns 'He looked at the straightedge in his hands' honestly; the cost is that the close's one designed pause moves from where the card put it, and the chapter's final turn now has two stage directions inside it instead of one. Lower severity than F04 because the packet's own closing_st
verified_findings.repair_target: Line 119 — move the dividers beat ahead of 'Now we find out how old the oldest one is.' and let the speech run to 'built the machine' unbroken.

verified_findings.gate: VOICE CHARTER §9 — repeated construction (a fresh phrase repeated is the same defect in a different coat)
verified_findings.evidence: in the fewest words a thing could be said in, which was how Brom said a thing that had cost him money
verified_findings.consequence: The identical frame — 'in the fewest words a thing could be told/said in' — is used twice inside one chapter, thirty-six lines apart, to characterise two different men's economy. It appears nowhere else in the twenty-four drafted chapters, so it is not house voice; it is a phrase the chapter invented and then reused, which flattens the distinction it is trying to draw between how Cael reports to Seln and how Brom prices bad news.
verified_findings.repair_target: Line 45 — recast Brom's economy in ledger terms of its own and leave the phrase to line 9.

verified_findings.gate: VOICE CHARTER §9 — repeated sentence scaffolds; Shared Positive Voice §Common failure modes
verified_findings.evidence: That was the whole of Lira's part, and it was, from Lira, the whole of the thing.
verified_findings.consequence: 'the whole of X' closes three beats in the circle movement (twice inside line 39's single sentence, again at line 57) and is joined at line 59 by 'the man's whole ledger for the night'. Five instances of the frame in the chapter; 118 across the drafted book. It is the voice's own gravity well rather than an imported tic, but used as a section-closer three times in fourteen lines it starts to announce section-ends rather than land them, and the strongest of the three (line 39, on Lira) loses force by being the first of a set.
verified_findings.repair_target: Line 57 — vary the closer for Brom and Cleon's exchange and let line 39 keep the frame.
